 1. None for the petitioners.
 2.

This petition has been filed praying for the following reliefs:
 "a) Rule be issued.
 b) Be pleased to issue writ of mandamus or writ in nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order and direction to adopt fair procedure such as lottery system etc. or any other procedure be provided for in respect of allotment of plots situated at gat no.
176 & 177 at Village-Padsali, Tal. Radhanagari, Dist. Kolhapur.

3. On 9 February, 2023, a co-ordinate Bench of this Court after hearing learned for the petitioners and learned AGP, had passed the following order:
"1. Mr. Kapse, learned counsel for the Petitioners invited our attention to some of the documents annexed to this petition at page Nos.21 to 59 in support of his submission that the Petitioner is already held eligible to get an alternate plot in the benefited zone under the provisions of Maharashtra Project Affected Persons Rehabilitation Act, 1999.

entities.text: Maharashtra Project Affected Persons Rehabilitation Act, 1999
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to the learned counsel for the Petitioners, the authority had pointed out the plot available in the benefited zone and though the Petitioners had identified said plot, same are illegally allotted to the other parties.

2. Mr. Pawar, learned AGP seeks time to consider the documents pointed out by the learned counsel for the Petitioners and to take instructions and make a statement before this Court whether the issue of eligibility of the Petitioners is already decided and if already decided, as to whether any alternate plot is allotted to the Petitioners,
and if not allotted, and if the Petitioners are already held eligible as to when the alternate plot under benefited zone would be allotted to the Petitioners.

3. Place this matter under the caption of 'Direction' on 14 th February, 2023 on supplementary board.
4. It is made clear that no further adjournment would be granted on the next date."

sentences.text:
Thereafter on 14 February, 2023, the co-ordinate Bench of this Court considering the contentions as urged on behalf of the petitioners and the State, was pleased to pass the following order:
"1. Mr. Kapse, learned counsel for the Petitioners states that the Petitioners and Mr.Manohar Keshav Shetye are entitled to the share in the compensation equally.

In support of this statement, he relied upon a letter dated 15th March, 2001 addressed by the Assistant Collector to Mr.Prabhakar Keshav Shetye and also a letter dated 21st September, 2001 from Wasudeo Keshav Shetye on behalf of Ramesh Wasudeo Shetye to the Assistant Collector.
We grant leave to the Petitioners to 14 June, 2023 5.WPST.3570_2023.DOC implead Mr.Manohar Keshav Shetye as one of the Respondent.
The amendment shall be carried out forthwith.
Re-verification is dispensed with.
The amendment shall also be carried out in the copies supplied to the Respondents.

2. An affidavit in reply filed by the Authority indicates that it is the stand of the Respondent Nos.1 to 5 that there is a dispute about the compensation between the family members of the Petitioners and more particularly paragraphs 2(vii) of the affidavit in reply, the Petitioners have not submitted their details and the proof of legal heirs.

3. The Petitioners as well as the newly added party are directed to remain present before the Sub Divisional Officer - Respondent No.1 on 27th February, 2023 at 11:00 a.m. with all requisite documents in support of their claim that they are entitled to 1/5th share in the total compensation in respect of the land under acquisition and also in support of their claim that each of them are entitled for separate alternate structure in lieu of the structures under acquisition.
The Petitioners have agreed to communicate this order to the newly added party for information and compliance.

4. The Respondent No.1 shall pass an order about the eligibility of each of these parties to get the compensation and further eligibility to get alternate structure in lieu of the structures which was the subject matter of land acquisition within four weeks from today.

Insofar, as the payment of 65%
compensation is required to be paid, if any, for allotment, since the compensation has not been distributed so far by the Competent Authority in favour of any of the Petitioners and the newly added party, the parties are entitled to make the submission before the Respondent No.1 for deduction of 65% amount from the compensation payable to each of them, if they are found eligible by the Respondent No.1 Authority.

If any submission is made by the Petitioners and the newly added party for deduction of 65% on their eligibility from the compensation, the Respondent No.1 to consider the said deduction and to pay the balance 35% of the amount within three months thereafter.
The Petitioners are at liberty to produce the consent affidavit of the newly added party before the Respondent No.1 at the time of hearing.

5. Place the matter on board for reporting compliance on 6th June, 2023."
5.
Thereafter on 23 February, 2023, time was extended to enable the petitioners to carry out amendment in terms of the order dated 14 February, 2023.
Accordingly, amendments were carried out.

entities.text: Shantaram Keshav Shetye And Ors vs The Sub-Divisional Officer And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering as to what has been observed by this Court in paragraphs 3 and 4 of the order dated 14 February, 2023, respondent no. 1 Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) was to hear the parties and pass an appropriate order on the eligibility of each of these parties to get the compensation and alternate structure in lieu of the structures which was the subject matter of land acquisition, within four weeks from the date of the said order.

7. In the aforesaid circumstances, we are of the opinion that if the order is not passed by the SDO, let the SDO pass an appropriate order after hearing all the parties including the added respondents.
The order be communicated to all the parties.
All contentions of the parties in that regard are expressly kept open.

8. The parties are free to take recourse to appropriate proceedings as permissible in law in the event any of the parties feel aggrieved by the order passed by the SDO.
9. Disposed of in the above terms.
No costs.

(RAJESH S. PATIL, J.) (G. S. KULKARNI , J.)
